utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Piletta-Zanin indicated before to us that he was not able to attend today. Ms. Pilipovic, are you ready to resume the cross-examination of the expert?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, will you please then guide the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Donia. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Donia, good day.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Donia, yesterday, in the course of our cross-examination, we discussed the conclusions arrived at within the framework of your expert report. Today, I would like to start out by asking you a couple of questions about the setting up of the national party, nationalist parties. You said that the three leading such parties won overwhelmingly at the first free elections; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us whether you have any knowledge as to the sequence of the setting up of those parties in the area of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were set up in two stages. They were set up, first of all, as founding committees in the period before the Supreme Court -- Constitutional Court decision made such parties legal. I do not know what order those three parties were established or those three committees were established. They were all essentially operating outside the law. The order of the actual founding assemblies which was the formal event, public event, kicking off the formation of the party, began, I believe, with the SDA; second was the HDZ; and third was the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Donia. As to the sequence of the setting up of these national parties, do you think it had any impact? What I mean to say, the fact that the first one to be set up was SDA, did it influence the setting up of the other nationalist parties afterwards?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe so, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we agree that the leader of the SDA was, and remained for a long time, Alija Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Isn't it correct that the party -- programme of that party was based on the Islamic declaration drawn up by Alija Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Have you had the opportunity to read the Islamic declaration?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Isn't it correct that the Islamic declaration is based on the conclusion about the fact that the Islam and Islamic [as interpreted] Institutions are irreconcilable [Realtime transcript read in error "reconcilable"]?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't know whether it is a translation problem, but the question as it presently framed does not make any sense.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It was irreconcilable, not "reconcilable" as we can see in the transcript. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Donia, if I tell you that one of the statements of the Islamic declaration -- well, I am going to try to interpret it and you can tell me whether I am correct or not, that the first and most important conclusion of each conclusion concerning the irreconcilability of Islam and non-Islamic institutions means that there can't be any peace or reconciliation between Islamic faith and non-Islamic institutions. Can you agree with this interpretation of the main idea of the Islamic declaration?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just interrupt. Does not mean that not only the word irreconcilable, but also Islamic and non-Islamic institution was in your first question because, as it reads now it says, that the Islam and Islamic institutions are reconcilable. So there are two corrections to be made. You are talking about the nonreconcilability --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] About the Islam and non-Islamic organisations not being reconcilable.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite the opposite. The Islamic declaration was written in the late 1960s precisely to reconcile the traditional, more fundamentalist positions of Islam at that time, with the modernizing Islamic states of that time represented principally then by the -- by Iran under the Shah. The purpose of that declaration, writing it, was in fact to address relations within Islam and between Islam and non-Islamic institutions and its purpose was clearly to reconcile those positions, not to put them in direct opposition.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So that's your interpretation. Mr. Donia, do you know that due to these attitudes, Mr. Alija Izetbegovic, in the course of the unity and brotherhood doctrine, was held responsible for that because his Islamic declaration at the time invited people to destroy the then common Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a false interpretation of both the declaration and the prosecution of Alija Izetbegovic, which took place in 1983, and I would not accept that as an accurate characterisation of what took place.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Donia, have you had the opportunity to read the ruling which condemned Mr. Alija Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: If, as the Defence counsel of General Galic, I present to you the incriminating evidence, rather, the indictment document leading to the ruling in that case, do you think you could still agree with me that, at that particular time, the attitudes expressed in the Islamic declaration called for the destruction of the common state?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The Islamic declaration made no mention of Bosnia-Herzegovina. The words never appear in the Islamic declaration. The word Yugoslavia never appears in the Islamic declaration. The Islamic declaration was addressed to the political situation everywhere else in the world, outside of Yugoslavia and Bosnia-Herzegovina. So, there was certainly an attempt by the Prosecution and, indeed, a ruling of the court that the ideas contained in the Islamic declaration constituted a danger for the political ideals then predominant in Bosnia-Herzegovina and Yugoslavia. But clearly such was not the case, as was argued quite successfully by the Defence in rejecting the claims of the Prosecution in that case.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence would like to present Mr. Donia with the sentence, and I would like to submit it as proof. We do have the text in English as well. There is a translation into English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you may present it to the witness, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just ask you that you prenumbered both D99, may I ask you that the English translation is D99.1, Ms. Pilipovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I do apologize.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Donia, can you see in front of you the ruling and, more specifically, page four of that text?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see on page 5 and within the framework of the indictment, that is to say, the allegations that Mr. Alija Izetbegovic and somebody else whose name I wouldn't like to mention - I don't know what the status of that person is - that the Islamic system of the unity of religion and politics?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't see where -- I am sorry, I don't see where you are -- perhaps we are dealing with the B/C/S, page 5.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Donia, on page 5. Thank you. On page five --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please, Ms. Pilipovic, indicate because of -- since we are using the English version, I see that there are some numbers now and then. So you are taking us to the...

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are taking us to the part which start with "early 1974"?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Afterwards on page 5, para 4, there is the indictment. From the declaration, the first and the most important conclusion must be the conclusion about the fact that the non-Islamic institutions and Islam are not reconcilable. That's something we have already presented to Mr. Donia. But then again on page six of the B/C/S version, and that means on page ten of the English version of the text, the last paragraph states: "In the text of the declaration in between the period of time between 1974 and 1983, with the aim of the counter-revolutionary threat to the social system of Yugoslavia and with the aim to set up the group of like-minded people within the country to pursue counter-revolutionary activities to destroy the social system," and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Donia, it is on page 10, the last paragraph in the English text.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And it might be a good idea for the interpreters to see the text as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are there any texts available for the interpreters as well, Ms. Pilipovic? Mr. Usher, could you please assist Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Donia, have you found the part of the text where it says that, "between 1973 and 1983." It is on page 10 of the English text.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you agree with me that in that particular period between 1974 and 1983, in view of the multi-ethnic composition of the population of Bosnia-Herzegovina, this declaration, any such message in fact, could have been characterised as a crime against the social system at that time, that is to say, the social system of the Republic of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under the communist era laws of that time, it was indeed possible to characterise this, the Islamic declaration, or just about any other political writing, as a crime against the state, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that the setting up of the SDA led by Mr. Alija Izetbegovic in the period of time around 1990 in the area of Bosnia-Herzegovina which still continued to exist as a multi-ethnic community could have, in relation to certain entities in that area, lead to a negative repercussions which were obviously reflected in the setting up of the nationalist parties and thus had an impact on the overall political and social situation in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would agree with most of that statement, but it is a very long and complicated set of hypotheses and I would not agree with all of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Donia. Mr. Donia, are you aware of the fact that on the 10th of June, 1991, in Bosnia-Herzegovina, there was a congress of Muslim intellectuals from all over Yugoslavia that passed a resolution that patriotic league was set up as well?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that the setting up of the patriotic league basically amounted to the setting up of party armed force?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Donia, can you agree with me that when it comes to the multi-ethnic community, such as Bosnia-Herzegovina used to be at the time, must needs disintegrate, if one party goes down the path of moving towards the dominant nation and when it comes to the defence issue on the basis of our discussions so far, that one entity would be the Muslim side because they were the majority and they had the opportunity to choose that option?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In your report you make a negative statements about the regionalisation of Bosnia-Herzegovina, advocated by the SDS party. As a historian and bearing in mind the national composition of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the setting up of the national party in Bosnia-Herzegovina, could you have reached any conclusions as to what could have led the Serb party to opt for a certain approach, regionalisation, that is?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I reached the conclusion and expressed in the report that this was the product of the SDS's desire to have political control by a single party and one nation, through the strategy of regionalisation.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And can you agree with me that it was proceeded by process of Islam-isation of Bosnia-Herzegovina according to the principles referred to in the Islamic declaration of Alija Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President,

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object to the question. It follows a number of questions by my learned colleague which probe the history of the politics of Bosnia-Herzegovina going well before 1990. Essentially, it seems probing an explanation of the events which occurred from around 1990 onwards. Mr. President, as I have indicated on previous occasions, the Prosecution does not seek to present to the Trial Chamber a view as to the lawfulness, or otherwise, of the armed conflict itself or to probe to any depth the contributing factors to that armed conflict. The purpose of this historical overview is to provide the Trial Chamber with the context which barely predates the commencement of the armed conflict itself, that is around 1990. Therefore, these questions raise the issue as to whether it is relevant to delve further back into the history. One could theoretically go back some 600 years. What, then, is the appropriate cut off point? Is it 1990? 1980, 1970 or so on? Mr. President, it seems to me that the guiding principle here is the extent to which the evidence is of assistance to the Bench in determining the specific issues that fall to it for determination and, from that perspective, it is my respectful submission that probing the social forces behind the political movement and the historical forces is of no assistance to the Trial Chamber. It simply isn't relevant. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: After having conferred with my colleagues in the Chamber, the Chamber has decided that the objection is denied. I think you have perfectly well put the question, Mr. Ierace, that how to find the very moment where to start, would that be 1990 or would it be 1988 or would there have to be September of 1992, that is not easy and therefore the Chamber thinks that it might not help a lot to go through the whole history of ages. Although it might give some explanation as well, but, the last question seemed to be very close to the starting point of the report. I think Ms. Pilipovic was asking the witness whether one of the events described in the report was preceded by another event and that is, in the opinion of the Chamber, is admissible. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Donia, do you know -- I apologise. In spite of the fact that having studied the transcript, I found out that you said that you weren't an expert in constitutional law, but first of all I would like to ask you whether you are familiar with the constitution of Bosnia-Herzegovina and I am talking about the 1990s, 1991?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the constitution of Bosnia-Herzegovina, in effect in 1990 and 1991, dated from 1974. I am generally familiar with its provisions, but would not claim to be a specialist in interpreting it or knowing intimately well.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: My question is only whether you are familiar with it. Did the constitution of Bosnia-Herzegovina provide for the possibility of regionalisation?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In your expert report, you stated that regionalisation was carried out according to the plan of the Serbian Democratic Party. Did you have the opportunity of becoming acquainted with this plan and could you tell us what it consisted of.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it consisted of several stages in different initiatives in different parts of the republic. It began in the Bosnian Krajina region in north-west Bosnia. In January, 1991, just weeks after the multi-party elections with a plan to associate the -- those municipalities in north-western Bosnia into a community of municipalities of the Bosnian Krajina. This plan came to partial fruition in April of 1991, and was subsequently ruled unconstitutional by the constitutional court of Bosnia-Herzegovina. It -- that is regionalisation took different forms in other parts of Bosnia-Herzegovina. It was the rationale for the withdraw of the municipality of Polje for the city of Sarajevo in early May of 1991 and was also used by SDS leaders in Herzegovina, and subsequently in other municipalities around Sarajevo, in Semberija -- they were both in western, not extreme western, in central Herzegovina and eastern Herzegovina and the Drina River area.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Donia, so you are telling us that the constitutional court with regard to the provision of Bosnia-Herzegovina which provided for the possibility of regionalisation, this court said it was unconstitutional. Could you tell us when this happened?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that the constitutional court declared unconstitutional, the association of the community of municipalities of the Bosnian Krajina. This happened I believe in the summer of 1991. I don't recall the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Donia. Mr. Donia, would you agree with me that there were problems between the peoples in the area of Bosnia-Herzegovina and that they were felt the most when the assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina was terminated on the 11th of September, 1991? And you have spoken about this in your report. It is on page five.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe I have a copy of my report here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are able to provide one to you.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We may again be looking at a different page where the translation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that Ms. Pilipovic is referring to page 4, approximately in the middle, where something is said on the -- she was referring to 11th of September.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the 15th of October, 1991, I apologise. In the B/C/S version, it is paragraph 2, right up at the beginning of page 5, where Mr. Donia spoke about the events of the 15th of October, 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... page three, Mr. Donia.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Donia, in this passage you mentioned a speech by Radovan Karadzic before the Assembly and you told us that he gave a speech saying that the Muslims could disappear as a whole if they declare the secessation of Bosnia-Herzegovina from Yugoslavia; he held this fierce speech?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that this part of his speech was related to the presentation -- was related to what they said could happen if war broke out?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have the opportunity to see the minutes from that Assembly or to have a look at a videorecording, and did you provide us with such an answer on the basis of this?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you agree that at that Assembly because of SDA and HDZ deputies who were -- spoke in an inappropriate way and spoke about the threat to the sovereignty, would you say that it is for this reason that the Assembly had to stop working?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us why the Assembly stopped working on that day?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It stopped working because it adjourned. I am not clear what your premise is here, but the Assembly in fact continued to meet quite regularly after this date well into -- well, throughout early 1992 and, in fact, beyond that. But I think I, as far as that date is concerned, outlined the primary events. It is actually the 14th of November and 15th of November when, following these exchanges, the Assembly was adjourned by its President Momcilo Krajisnik --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- of the SDA and HDZ subsequently reconvened the session and passed the declaration of sovereignty.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Donia. I just wanted to ask you to confirm something and to give me this answer, that the delegates of the HDZ and the SDA passed a declaration on sovereignty? Mr. Donia, are you aware that the decisions of the Assembly could be passed only with the participation of all of the three constituent peoples, that is to say, all the three bodies of the Assembly?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you think that this decision by the deputies of the HDZ and SDA without the participation of the SDS deputies, do you think that such a decision is a legitimate and constitutional, according to the constitution that was valid at the time?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot make the judgment on whether this was a constitutionally valid decision or not, either by virtue of the constitution or the rules of the procedure of the Assembly. I only know that the provision for a sovereign Bosnia-Herzegovina was already a part of the constitution from amendments passed in February of 1990.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just for my better understanding ask one question, Ms. Pilipovic. From the report, I read that, "It was on the 15th of October, 1991 that Mr. Karadzic delivered a speech," and then the report continues, "and after the Assembly had adjourned for the day by its SDS President Momcilo Krajisnik and the Bosnian Serb delegation had departed, HDZ and SDS delegates reconvened the session and passed the declaration of sovereignty." When I read it this way, it looks as if it was on the same day, but I see in your testimony now that you are referring to the 14th and the 15th of November for the declaration of sovereignty was made, and I wondered whether this was a mistake or I was not able to read properly what it said. If you look at page 14, line 25. It will soon disappear.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think that it is a mistake. I think that Mr. Donia mentioned those two dates at one point in time but I think that we have agreed after all that we are only speaking about the 15th of October, 1991. Mr. Donia can correct me if I am wrong.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, Mr. President, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Donia, was leaving the Assembly by -- was the Serbian deputies leaving the Assembly after this unconstitutional declaration of sovereignty, do you consider that this was a legitimate act on their part? Because of the protection of the interest of the Serbian people, was it legitimate to leave this Assembly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the question assumes that the Serbian deputies left the Assembly after the declaration. I am not sure that that is the evidence of this witness. Perhaps that could be clarified first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. In the English transcript, Ms. Pilipovic, it reads: "Was leaving the Assembly by the Serbian deputies -- leaving the Assembly after this unconstitutional declaration of sovereignty." Was that your question, since the -- at least the report, and as far as I understand the testimony, was that they left and that only afterwards the declaration of sovereignty was proclaimed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. There was a slight misunderstanding. I shall rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Donia, do you think that -- Mr. Donia, could you confirm that the passing of the declaration of sovereignty was an unconstitutional decision?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not qualified to assess its constitutionality. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree, Mr. Donia, that after the adoption, after the passing on the declaration of sovereignty, all ties which were based on national relations were suspended or broken? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And do you think that the decision to form the Assembly of the Serbian People and all other institutions, was this a legitimate decision given the right of the people to determine itself to self-determination?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I am not able to render a judgment on its constitutionality.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know anything about the fact that when the Serbian people passed other decisions, do you know whether they took those decisions, passed those decisions with full respect for the rights of the people to self-determination?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what you mean by "Serbian people." And I would ask maybe that you clarify what -- if there is a particular deliberative body that you have in mind or what the "Serbian people" constituted. I am not clear on the import of the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I apologise. Your Honour, the Defence has a decision. These are the records from the Assembly of the Serbian people of the 21st of November, 1991. This is a document which the Defence obtained from the Prosecution. I would like to show part of this record, part of these minutes, but I first would like to ask Mr. Donia a question.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Donia, did you have the opportunity of becoming acquainted with the contents of the minutes of the Assembly of the Serbian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina which were held in Sarajevo on the 21st of November, 1991.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that this is an assembly which was held after the plebiscite of the Serbian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina with regard to their declaration on whether they would like to remain within Bosnia-Herzegovina within the context of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have the opportunity while you were examining the minutes, did you have the opportunity to become familiar with the speech of the President of the Assembly at that time, Mr. Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did, and I could not recite it to you from memory but I became familiar with it in the course of preparing this report, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: If from the Assembly, if from the minutes of the Assembly of the Serbian People I quote a part of Mr. Krajisnik's statement: "We want to inform all peoples in Bosnia-Herzegovina that we want to preserve a unified Bosnia-Herzegovina. Our desire is to live together but in peace -- with love and with peace."

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps, pursuant to the usual agreement, my friend could provide me a copy of that document, ideally before it is read out but in this case --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see that in footnote 10 of the report reference is made a meeting of the Assembly of the Serbian People of Bosnia-Herzegovina of the 21st of November, 1991. I don't know whether this is a complete shorter note of the meeting, but perhaps you could guide us because it is quite a lot of pages at least. I see --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- both an English and an B/C/S version of that document which is, I could tell you --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence has prepared a speech -- the speech from page 11 in the B/C/S version, and in the English version, 009301. I have enough -- I have sufficient copies of that part of the record and I am prepared to provide it to my colleagues. I have marked it as number 100, evidence for the Defence. I hope I have a sufficient number of copies for the interpreters, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but if it is part of the other meeting, is it any use to have a repetitious -- to have the same document again?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I have just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... last three digits, but perhaps distributed, perhaps it should not be tendered but we have it available. But could you tell us the last three digits of the English version so that Mr. Ierace and the Chamber are able to follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your Honour, the last three digits of the English version are 301. I think that 3 -- I think in B/C/S those are pages 11, 12 and 16.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Donia, do you have a copy from the 2nd Assembly -- Session of the Serbian People?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: On the first page of the English version, in the third paragraph, Mr. Krajisnik said that, "The main principle which should be adhered to in our activities -- " I apologise. "The main principal that we should adhere to in our activities is not to impose the will of the Serbian people on other peoples. We should respect the justified will of the Muslim and the Croatian people, but we must not underestimate our advantages too, which expressed in the real relation of political forces in Bosnia-Herzegovina and we must not give up our rights to others." Mr. Donia, from this part that I have just read, can one draw the conclusion that the Serbian people want to carry on living together in a unified Bosnia-Herzegovina, but in Yugoslavia, too?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only if one takes this paragraph in isolation from other statements made in resolutions passed at this session.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I am having some difficult locating the relevant passage in the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Page 301, last three digits. Yes, it is, I would say, the third paragraph of that page, "the basic principle you should observe," and then for the next four or five lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have additional copies for the interpreters, Ms. Pilipovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have tried to make a sufficient number of copies, but it is obvious that I don't have enough copies. I apologise. I really made an effort in order to be as efficient as possible and to ensure that we could work as fast as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course, the Judges could provide the Serbian -- the B/C/S version of the -- I don't know whether that might help some of you. So that we just mark the office's, the B/C/S version. I could provide the B/C/S version as well. I think we can use this document because since it is already part of the filing of the footnotes of Mr. Donia's report. So, I usually would not, I would prefer not to split up documents. It is not of a major problem here, perhaps. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Donia, I think that you agreed with this paragraph we have just read out, but that you made a comment and that you said that you would not agree with it in relation to certain other discussions. As far as you can remember, with reference to this session, were there any significant divisions of use with regards to such viewpoints which the President of the Assembly expressed at the time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, may I ask you - and you perhaps as well, Mr. Donia - since translation needs some time, to slow down a bit. Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Assembly itself was in the process of taking actions which contradicted this statement. I cited this document in the first instance for its confirmation of the establishment of regions dominated by Serbs and by the SDS in the strategy of taking those regions outside of the jurisdiction of the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina. There are other parts of Mr. Krajisnik's speech which suggest, in fact, that this is a highly conditional assurance that is easily abrogated. If we go, for example, to the next page, 0302, I am looking at the English in the formulation that is about halfway down the page, "If we separate in peace, we have a chance to associate again in the future. If we go to war, I don't believe we will ever do that. On our way to achieving the goals of the Serbian people, we accept all friends, we accept everybody, except traitors and opponents."

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Donia, is this in contradiction with the statements with reference to the desire and the willingness of the Serb people to continue to live in a unified Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, according to your opinion, why?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The creation of the Serbian autonomous regions or SAO's was specifically an act of dismembering the authority of the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Donia, it does seem to me that we had agreed that it is the legitimate right of every people to have the right to self-determination, if it is guaranteed by all international conventions and charters. Why do you think that the right of the Serb people to self-determination at that particular time and the wish, once again I reiterate, to remain within a unified Bosnia-Herzegovina is unacceptable?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object to the question, in particular the first few words. It does seem to me that we had agreed that it is a legitimate right and so on. I don't know what my friend has in mind in relation to that. Perhaps, you could clarify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please, before answering the question, Mr. Donia, tell us whether you and Ms. Pilipovic have agreed or would agree that it is the legitimate right of every people to have the right of self-determination, as guaranteed in all international conventions and charters, because that was the assumption of the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, more specifically, my learned colleague asked the witness whether he agreed that certain acts done by the SDA party, in particular the declaration of sovereignty, was unconstitutional. She then followed that by asking him whether, in his opinion, certain acts taken by the Serbian party were a legitimate expression of the right to self-determination, as I recollect it. And that is the only reference that I recollect in relation to the right of self-determination. So that's specifically my concern, that this question doesn't seem to rise from the answers given to those questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is an assumption of which the question starts with an assumption. Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, perhaps Mr. Donia can correct me, but I believe that we did agree when we referred to the legitimate right of self-determination of all peoples. I believe we agreed on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you believe, Mr. Donia, that all peoples have the legitimate right to self-determination? I mean, I can't really --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, we have dealt with two issues. The 1st issue is, I think, the constitutional right to self-determination and in your question now, you are referring to the right of self-determination of peoples and the international legal instruments, which might be a different thing. So, would you please first clarify on what issues you and Mr. Donia would agree and on what issues not. Because it seems to cover two different aspects of self-determination of peoples. I mean, are we talking about the Yugoslav peoples, the Narod, or are we talking about peoples in the context of public international law? Please proceed. Or do you have any --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, I can assist, Mr. President. The question was asked at page 16, line 13 of the English transcript. There was an objection to the question. The question was never answered. Mrs. Pilipovic then said she would rephrase the question and asked something entirely different, that is, the question to whether the leaving of the Assembly by the Serbian deputies was a legitimate act on their part, and I think that's the reference to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it was legitimacy under the constitution rather than under instruments of public international. I think Ms. Pilipovic quite understood where the problems are and she certainly will clarify that question.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Donia, can you confirm whether according to the constitution at the time the constitutional peoples - and we do know that there were three constitutional people in Bosnia-Herzegovina - so whether, according to the constitution at the time, they had the right to self-determination. Can you answer that question?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the constitution of Bosnia-Herzegovina of 1974, the three constituent nations were accorded the right of self-determination, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Donia, we are still discussing the assembly meeting of the Serb Assembly of the 21st of November, 1991. You disagreed with Mr. Krajisnik's statement made at that Assembly, and can you tell us about the decision of the members of that Assembly on that day, the 24th of November, after the referendum?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be clear, I didn't disagree with Mr. Krajisnik's statement. I objected to the context or your failure to cite the appropriate context in which that statement was made and the many other statements that contributed it within that same meeting. I don't know what decision you are referring to on the Assembly of 24th of November, 1991. I think there were several decisions reached on that day. But if you could be more specific, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Donia, if I tell you that two decisions were made, the first one being to approve the results of the referendum of the Serb people which was held on the 9th of November. I do apologise: Once again, it is on the last page of the minutes of that meeting. Once again, the Assembly meeting of the 21st of November. I believe it must be the last page in the English text as well. The second decision says: "It is confirmed that the decision of the Serbian people of Bosnia-Herzegovina to remain in the common state of Yugoslavia adopted by the Assembly of the Serbian People in Bosnia-Herzegovina at its session of the 24th of October, 1991 is hereby upheld by the plebiscite of the Serbian People held on the 9th and the 10th of November, 1991, and that the same has come in to effect." So, Mr. Donia, can you agree with me that the Assembly is made up of delegates of the MPs and that they -- the main point is their reaching the decisions, and decision is something that I referred to when I was talking about the statement made by the President of the Assembly. Can you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First, Ms. Pilipovic, you are indicating that we can find this on the last page of the -- that is 311.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. That is para 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Donia, can we agree that the Parliament or the Assembly is a body where everybody is free, all the delegates are free, to voice their views but the basic opinion of the Assembly as a whole is reflected in the decision and the decision is the one that we just read?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Donia, can you agree with me that the views of the SDA and HDZ parties at the time when the referendum of the Serb people was being held continued to be the sovereignty and that in that case the Serb people would have become a minority?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is two questions as I hear you ask them. Did the SDA and HDZ parties continue to support the position of the sovereignty of Bosnia-Herzegovina? Yes, they did. Would, in that case, the Serb people become a minority? No, it wouldn't change the position of the Serbian -- those of Serbian nationality and Bosnia-Herzegovina in any way.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And can you agree with me that already at that time Serbs in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and especially in Sarajevo, were not getting equal treatment in all institutions, universities and even hospital?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Donia, in your footnotes you referred to the minutes of the Serb autonomous region of Romanija of the 18 -- 11th of December, 1991. I am just going to try to find the footnote here. It is footnote number 23, I believe. Have you had the opportunity to actually read through the minutes of that meeting, the Serb Assembly of the autonomous region of Romanija?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe it is footnote 23.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Footnote 23 is a law, Ms. Pilipovic, in Croatia, in the municipality of Rajlovac.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Might it be 13? 12 or 13?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 13 relates to the --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, 13. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We agree on that, anyway.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence has the minutes of that particular meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Donia, have you had the opportunity to read through the minutes?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that there was statement, a public statement, made at the end of that Assembly on the 11th of December, 1991? I am going to --

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I can give you a copy and I've got enough copies in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask the usher to provide the interpreters with the English texts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you, Ms. Pilipovic, help me in finding -- I will wait until I have a look at the English so that I can find them in my binder of footnotes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is the last page. Your Honour, the footnote is number 13, the minutes of the meeting, and the page is 286 in the English translation and in the B/C/S version it is the last page of the minutes. But I don't see whether it is numbered -- oh, yes it is. 3692.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I may assist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: As I indicated yesterday, the Prosecution has prepared some binders of the documents as it transpired. Mr. President, you said that it was not necessary but the fact is, they have been done with tabs, which we couldn't have done with the filed version. I wonder whether those long hours could be put to use at some stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You didn't tell me that you added tabs, Mr. Ierace, and if I would have known that, the Chamber would have approached the matter totally differently.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Within five minutes, Mr. President, I anticipate we can have three sets brought down. In the meantime, perhaps I could hand up some indexes for those volumes which are coming. And they will assist in finding the appropriate tab. I will hand up three indexes and we will bring down the set, of course, for my learned colleague, an index for my learned colleague.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Donia, can you see the minutes in front of you, the minutes of the autonomous district of Romanija of the 11th of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: To my question as to whether the Serb people would end up being a minority if the referendum was -- were held according to the attitudes as the HDZ, well, you have replied, no, and as to whether they would get an equal treatment, what do you think about that? Do you know anything about whether they would have had any equal treatment within certain institutions?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first part of your question has mischaracterised my answer to an earlier question. I think we talked about whether the Serbian people would become a minority in view of the sovereignty of Bosnia-Herzegovina. You instead suggested that I answered that question in terms of the referendum. The referendum, as you know, at this time had not yet been held or even scheduled.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I do apologise. Yes. Thank you. What we are discussing is simply the status of the Serb people. So, your reply is they would not have been treated as a minority?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they would have continued in all likelihood to have been -- continued -- treated, to be treated as a constituent nation.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And if I tell you that already at that time the Serb people was not being given equal treatment in all institutions, starting from universities and all the way down to hospitals, can you tell me whether you have any knowledge of such an atmosphere and that sort of attitude towards Serbs at that time, of course?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no knowledge of such attitudes or policies, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Donia, if I tell you that the Assembly of the Serb Autonomous district of Romanija, on the day of the 11th of December 1991, made a statement where it is said that the Assembly of Romanija at its meeting, amongst other things, reached a decision to tell the public about rough discrimination against Serb patients when they were hospitalised in Sarajevo and that was the behaviour on the part of non-Serb doctors and other staff. The same sort of treatment was admitted at to Serb students at the Sarajevo University on the part of non-Serb professors. That not only went against the ethical principles of those professions but it is a kind of thing that may lead to ethnic tensions. As far as you are concerned, do you believe that such a statement from such a body is acceptable, bearing in mind the events that preceded that period and the conditions under which this Assembly was held?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a typical complaint of extreme nationalists at this time. And I know of no foundation for these complaints or allegations. I see no evidence in these minutes of specific incidents or policies which would validate the allegation contained in this public declaration.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Donia, on what basis can you claim that the members of the Assembly of the Autonomous District of Romanija -- well, you said that this was a decision that could have only been passed by an extremist body. Well, can you tell us on the basis of what you reach that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that such grievances were typical of extreme nationalists, and I would add extreme nationalists on all sides, in this time of this kind of abuse at the hands of social or governmental institutions.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you are telling us that you have no knowledge of any such lack of an equal treatment when it same to the Serbs in the various institutions in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I have no knowledge of anything that would support these particular allegations and I see no specific information or allegations rendered in the minutes of this meeting, in support of these very general allegations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President. I just want to make the point that during the cross-examination of two doctors, one being a Serb from a state hospital, it was not put to either doctor by my learned colleague that there had been such behaviour on the part of doctors towards patients prior to the war. I simply wish to draw to the attention of the Trial Chamber at this stage. Perhaps later I will make it relevant to general submissions under Rule 90. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. As far as I know, a witness was heard by this Chamber. I don't know whether it was a protected witness, but it was gentleman who did not say he was a Serb. Maybe his name and family name indicated he might have been a Serb, but we never ever asked any of the witnesses what their nationality was, at least not to the best of my recollection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that Mr. Ierace is pointing to -- drawing our attention to the fact that when doctors who are treating patients in hospitals were heard that no question, as on the factual basis of the allegations we are dealing with at this moment, no questions were put to them in that respect.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, at that time, we were cross-examining witnesses or, rather, there was the examination-in-chief and that referred to 1992 up until August 1994. The document in the possession of the Defence and that Mr. Donia has referred to, is a document from 1991. So we are discussing the possession or rather the treatment that referred to the period of time prior to the outbreak of the hostilities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is denied. There might be given several reason for that, but one of them is that the situation prior to the period that is covered by the indictment is specifically dealt with in the report of Mr. Donia which was not available at that time to the Defence. So, therefore when the issue has been to some extent been introduced by the report, the situation prior to the -- I would say the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. outbreak of the armed conflict, and therefore you may proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Donia, can you agree that at that time by the end of 1991 and the beginning of 1992, the international community came up with a whole range of different solutions to the crisis in Bosnia-Herzegovina? Well, more specifically, I just like to remind you of a couple of cases, and this actually is my question: Could you clarify the so-called Cutilhiero plan for Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well that's much later than this document. We are moving on to 1990 -- 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I think it was in February, 1992. Yes, Mr. Donia.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the international community became involved in the period over the change of the new year via the Badinter Commission first and subsequently as a part of the international conference on the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you believe that the Cutilhiero plan was based on the regionalisation of all three peoples within the BH, within the framework of Yugoslavia? Do you have any knowledge of that?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was effectively a plan for the division of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that Mr. Alija Izetbegovic withdrew his initial statement after signing the Cutilhiero plan?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And can you agree with me if I tell you that Mr. Alija Izetbegovic withdrew his signature and that that was the reason why the Cutilhiero plan so to say was never implemented?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is partly correct, but there are some events prior to that which essentially doomed the Cutilhiero plan from being implemented.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, if you can find a suitable moment for a break.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think this is the appropriate moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will adjourn until quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: --- Upon resuming at 4.17 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, are you ready to proceed?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Donia, before the break, we were speaking about the essence of Cutilhiero's plan, which appears to have been the best solution for Bosnia-Herzegovina, which unfortunately was not accepted. But in your expert report, on page 6 of that report, footnote number 26, you spoke about a document; you referred to a document of the Serbian democratic party on the organisation or activity of the Serbian people. If it is of any help, the page is 00184274 of the B/C/S version and the English version is 0035993. I have a copy of one of the pages from that document. I don't know that it is necessary now to provide you with these copies since we all have that document, with the exception of Mr. Donia.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, do you need a copy of this document also or do you have it?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think I have that document. I am locating it now. Mr. President, the ERN number for the English version in the transcript lacks a final number. Perhaps that might be clarified. It reads 0035993. I think there should be one more number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it is -- the document ends with "6," so 936, and due to your tabs, Mr. Ierace, I found it already. It is in the second binder, first tab, 2631. Yes. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Donia, you have a document in front of you. Those are the instructions for the organization and activity of organs of the Serbian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina in extraordinary circumstances?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: As part of this document -- with reference to this document, you spoke about the organisation of the SDS and you spoke about the A and B Variants. In your footnotes 27 and 28, you made reference to this?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that at that time it was normal to act in a unified way when forming a government?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Is it for that reason that these instructions on the organisation and activity of the Serbian people were passed, that is as is mentioned here, in extraordinary circumstances?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not clear that that is the reference that the document is suggesting. But I would agree that these were extraordinary circumstances, and for that matter, extraordinary times.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Donia, under item 8 of this document, on page 5 of the translation, page 2620 or 0035940, that is the ERN number in English, item 8 states: "In following all these measures, take care to ensure that the national and other rights of members of all peoples are respected. At a later time ensure that they are involved in the government bodies that will be set up by the Assembly of the Serbian people in the municipality. Mr. Donia, would you agree with me that these instructions -- now that I have read out item 8 from this document, would you agree that these instructions were in no way detrimental to other peoples?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us what you mean by "no?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This statement that you have read number 8 in the, I believe the second stage, the final set of instructions, is the only statement in this document that even in the broadest sense hints that there will be regard for other peoples. This document is a blueprint, in fact, to prepare for and go to war. It is a blueprint for the establishment and ultimately activation of separate Serbian institutions under SDS control, prepared and carried out in secret, and intended to establish single party one nation control over all institutions in the country.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us on what basis you have arrived at this conclusion, on the basis of which documents?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think if you look at the document as a whole, it is self-evidently a blueprint for a seizure of power.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that when we are dealing with extraordinary circumstances, when this is at stake, in such cases the process of organising the people and the process of operation of the organs of power at the levels of municipalities and of other institutions, would you agree that this is also organised in other parts of Bosnia-Herzegovina? Let me simplify this. Are such instructions, in your opinion, on the organisation in extraordinary circumstances, would this be acceptable if all three entities are at issue in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, may I ask you one thing? Very often a question of yours starts with, "Would you agree with me" and then there comes a whole complex of what Mr. Donia would have to answer, whether he would agree or not. Could you please split up, because we have several times heard the answer, "no," and at least we know that he does not agree with all that you said. Sometimes he makes a distinction between partially yes and partially no. But wouldn't it be more efficient if you would split up sometimes and see whether on certain issues he would agree with you, so that the Chamber gets the information the Chamber very much would like to have. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Donia, you are telling us that the party of Democratic Action and the HDZ when Bosnia-Herzegovina was in extraordinary circumstances, when it found itself in such a situation, these parties did not organise and provide instructions to their people, issue instructions to their people in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There, to my knowledge, has never been instructions of this character issued by either of the other two parties, national parties. In the extent of their specificity, the particular steps to be taken, all of which were implemented carefully - in some places with considerable opposition - in the number of municipalities as instructed, no, there is nothing comparable that I know of that has ever been shown to have been characteristic of the other two parties.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you give us an example --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, General Galic would like to have some contact with you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I heard what he said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was just worrying about whether the communication --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Microphone, please

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your microphone is off. We can't hear you, General Galic. The microphone is off. If you want to communicate with Ms. Pilipovic, that is perfect. If you want to address the Chamber, then please put it on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said several things but now I will just say thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take the opportunity to -- General Galic, you are facing to the back of Ms. Pilipovic, so if there is ever a moment where you would like to communicate when she doesn't see it, don't hesitate to put on your microphone and ask for a moment to confer with counsel. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour. I have understood you very well and thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Donia, if in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina at that time there were two parties in operation, the HDZ and the SDA, and they were operating in the coalition and the declaration was passed on the sovereignty, in such a case, is it justified -- is the organisation of the Serbian people justified in such extraordinary circumstances?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot envision the circumstances under which it would be justified to establish separate governmental institutions, secure secret places for hiding provisions, declaring separate institutions and seizing power from regular governmental institutions in nearly all the local communities of a country. And that is what these instructions are. They are not a simple legislative act or a declaration of principles; they are very specific instructions for preparing to seize power and for seizing power. And it's, as I say, difficult for me to envision the circumstances that would justify such action. Certainly, such circumstances did not exist in Bosnia on 19 December, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Donia, but in your report on page six when you mentioned the variants and you explained the explanations of the 19th of December, the instructions of the 19th of December, 1991, you told us that the main committees of the SDS are different in the municipalities where the Serbs are in the majority. In this case, is it logical if in one municipality one of the parties got the majority; was it logical for them to organise power there?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think those organisational activities that had already taken place in all municipalities and had been carried out in accord with agreement among the three parties that prevailed in the November 1990 elections. So this is not a case of organising a municipality. That had already taken place. The legitimate governmental institutions were already well in place. This was a plan to establish parallel institutions and ultimately to overthrow the existing legal governmental institutions as they existed on this date.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Donia, you don't accept that the Serbian people had the right to self-determination, according to the constitution of Bosnia-Herzegovina? You do not accept that they had the right to organise their own bodies of power, organs of power.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your first proposition is a totally different one than is addressed in this document and which we have been speaking. As to whether they served, representatives had the right to organise their own bodies of power, from a constitutional standpoint, I can't make that judgment. This document makes no effort to argue that it conforms in any way with any constitution.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: That is your opinion?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Donia, in footnote 46, 80 and 11, I will read out part of the footnote. On footnote 46, on page 8, where you referred to the shorthand notes of the session of the people of Serbian, in footnote 46 from the record of this Assembly, you came -- on the basis of that record, you came to the conclusion that some Bosnian Serbs fought with the JNA and with the local Serbs in Croatia as well as with as members of the JNA and as volunteers who organised by activists of the SDS and various municipalities?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us on the basis of which part of the record you came to this conclusion?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the -- I believe I gave the ERN number of that Assembly session in which there is what amounts to a bragging contest about how each municipality has contributed troops to the war effort in support of the Serbs in Croatia. I see only the English ERN, but I believe that section is the place where that discussion is held. There is plenty of other evidence concerning the role of Bosnian Serbs as well as volunteers in Croatia. I here have only drawn attention to the quote of Romanija and the appropriate celebration in Han Pijesak simply because those are most relevant to the Sarajevo area.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think the B/C/S ERN is indicated immediately following the tab which reads "11, 46, 80." The ERN for both English and B/C/S is given on the first page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I have seen that. But I think the B/C/S indication is to a specific page of that ending 663, if I am correct, line 663. So I was just trying to assist Ms. Pilipovic in order to find whether I could trace where line 663 as it should be approximately, I would say, some 15 pages from the -- but that would be more in B/C/S, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with regard to this -- these notes, the Defence would appreciate it if Mr. Donia could tell us on the basis of whose speech he came to such a conclusion. And I would like to ask Mr. Donia, within the framework of these notes from the Assembly, was the subject of national interest discussed at all, that it would be in the national interest to leave the state of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have the opportunity of reading the speech of Mr. Alex Buha and other participants in this assembly?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's two questions. The first one is very specific as to -- I am looking at footnote 46. I assume that's the question at issue since I use the word "only one delegate." I would have to look at the --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It seems to be in the English version on page 27. The name seems to be Tosic who said, "I also want to draw attention of my honourable colleague, Mr. Brdjanin, to the fact that the Serbian people..." And that's what I see in your footnote 46. So, that would be page 27 of the English version and it would be -- now it becomes more difficult. I think it is page 55, but I am not quite sure. Yes, that must be page 55 in the B/C/S version, Ms. Pilipovic, where I see the name Tosic and it starts with as far as I can read "Mr. President," and then the second part at least it is referring to "Kolega Brdjanin". I think that is the part the witness is referring to.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. President, I am handicapped by not having the documents in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I was just about to suggest --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in order to save time, I shall withdraw this question, so that we don't have to try and find this in the transcript. Because if Mr. Donia can't remember who said that -- but he did state or someone did state that a deputy stated this. I will ask another question with regard to these notes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you look at page 55, Ms. Pilipovic, you'll almost certainly find that same words. Yes, it speaks about a Srpski Narod Romanija. That must be the Serbian people.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I found it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Donia, on the basis of what Mr. Tosic, the deputy, said at this Assembly, you came to this conclusion in footnote 46 on this basis. I think that you've actually quoted this part in your footnote; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Donia, were there any other speakers at that Assembly having views different from those of Mr. Tosic?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall that -- I do recall that there was a suggestion that the Romanija Serbs were under-represented. That was made by, I believe, Mr. Brdjanin, but the suggestion was made by another speaker and that was the comment that elicited this refutation and claimed that, "a good number of our people were involved in some of the critical battles in Croatia."

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Donia, have you had the opportunity to read through the minutes referring to the statement by Mr. Buha? It is on page seven.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am sorry. I am still not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you have binder two in front of you -- no. Let me just sort of --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have one, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One is okay. It would then be the -- I think it's the fourth tab which says 11, 46, 80.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And what page is this --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is on page 7. It is the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would that be page 3? Professor Aleksa -- is that the speaker you are referring to, Ms. Pilipovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have that, Ms. Pilipovic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you agree that Mr. Buha's statement was in contradiction to what certain other speakers have said, you yourself referred to Mr. Tosic? Now, I would like to know whether on page 7, Mr. Buha - it is at the bottom of the page - didn't he say that, "This historical crossroads, the Muslim and the Croat peoples, will have to provide answers to some questions. Have they recognised that leaving the Republic of Yugoslavia is not something that the Serb people is going to be violently opposed to for the sake of the country, but they want to make sure that the territory that they occupy remains in the rump Yugoslavia"?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you agree that the substance, the aim and the desire of the Serb people was their right to decide to remain within Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the critical issue for most Serbs, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Have you when analysing this documentation pertaining to the Assembly meetings of the Serb people, been able to conclude that, for the most part, the speakers did not speak out against the wishes of the other two constituent peoples to act in line with their right of self-determination, but they just wanted the same right to apply to them? When I say "them," I mean the Serb people.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first -- there's two questions I hear you asking. I think the first is: Did most speakers not speak out against the wishes of the other two constituent peoples? And I would say yes, that is the case. The rights to which the Serbs, Serbian speakers at the Assembly, were referring, however, went far beyond the rights that they would attribute to the other two constituent peoples.
